# Opal Pettigrew

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P5](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0005)</sub>
- **Status:** deceased  <sub>[v3 c14 P7](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0007), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Role:** Prospective schoolteacher  <sub>[v3 c11 P53](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0053), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002)</sub>

## Appearance

Opal possessed striking, high-colored beauty with a bright complexion and radiant eyes and cheeks. She was especially noted for her gorgeous, long yellow hair braids, which she wore pinned around her head. Towards the end of her life, her face turned wan and pale, though she retained a cheerful and vivid appearance before her illness fully overtook her.

_Sources: [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v3 c11 P52](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0052), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P5](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0005)_

## Personality

Opal was vibrant, talkative, and persistent in maintaining a cheerful and optimistic exterior even when ill. She enjoyed lively social gatherings, summer gowns, and chatting about her prospective suitors and their rivalries. Beneath her cheerful facade, she harbored a deep fear of dying and an intense dread of facing the unfamiliarity of the afterlife.

_Sources: [v3 c11 P52](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0052), [v3 c11 P53](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0053), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013)_

## Goals

- teach school at Pale Sands  <sub>[v3 c11 P53](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0053)</sub>

## History

Opal grew up in Brierley and attended school alongside local youth such as Nell Harcourt, Isolde Pembroke, and Odette Pullen. During one midsummer game at Pembroke's pond, she joined her friends in dramatizing Tennyson's Elaine, though she refused to lie still in the flat out of fear. She later planned to teach school at Pale Sands, though her failing health forced her to postpone her plans until the new year. Throughout her final summer, she hosted visitors at the Pettigrew house and spent many evenings conversing with Nell in her garden. In her final quiet evening with Nell, Opal admitted her deep fear of death and the unfamiliarity of heaven. She passed away peacefully in her sleep the following morning, leaving an incomplete piece of embroidery behind for Nell.

_Sources: [v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001), [v1 c28 P7](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0007), [v3 c11 P52](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0052), [v3 c11 P53](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0053), [v3 c14 P0](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0000), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030), [v3 c14 P33](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0033)_
